page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-48 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on x86_64 architecture using Intel processors. The instance provides 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores with two hardware threads per core. Memory allocation totals 96.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The underlying processor configuration features a 260 MB shared L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1 data cache per core. Hardware-level acceleration features include AVX-512 extensions (f, vnni, bf16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8), along with hardware-assisted cryptographic primitives such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark measurements indicate strong multi-core processing capability and memory throughput. The instance achieves top-quartile performance in multi-core Geekbench testing (17,375.0) and PassMark CPU evaluations (58,467.72), with notable strengths in CPU encryption, physics calculations, and extended instructions. Memory subsystems sustain large-block uncached read speeds of 276.52 GB/sec and write speeds of 118.36 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25 percent for memory bandwidth. Application-level metrics highlight strong database processing (26,021.35 on PassMark) and high static web serving throughput of 68.79 GB/sec. In contrast, single-core execution metrics, such as stress-ng single-core (1,680.69) and Geekbench single-core (1,862.0), reside in the median performance bracket.

Hardware tradeoffs are evident in storage and accelerator provisions. The configuration includes zero GPUs and provides no complimentary local storage, necessitating external network-attached volumes for persistent data. While prompt processing for smaller and medium language models is competitive via AMX acceleration, large-scale generation shows degraded throughput, such as 2.71 tokens per second on 70B parameter models. Qualitative cost efficiency is favorable for parallel, CPU-bound workloads that do not require extensive memory footprints or attached accelerators, making it a targeted solution for parallel batch jobs, web fleets, Clang builds, and distributed database nodes.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-48 is a compute-oriented virtual machine configured with 48 dedicated Intel x86_64 vCPUs across 24 physical cores and 96.0 GB of system memory. Operating at a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, the instance integrates 260 MB of L3 cache along with advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-quartile multi-core processing, CPU encryption, and large-block uncached memory throughput reaching 276.52 GB/sec read and 118.36 GB/sec write. It also maintains strong results in static web serving throughput and relational database operations. The platform bundles no local storage and lacks discrete GPUs, meaning persistent storage depends wholly on external storage volumes. Given its 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation, the instance maximizes efficiency for compute-intensive tasks, parallel CI/CD compilation, web server fleets, and distributed data processing rather than memory-heavy or large-scale AI generation workloads.
